verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.200
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 5.200

verses.pali: 20. Brāhmaṇavagga
verses.english: 20. Brahmins

verses.pali: Nissāraṇīyasutta
verses.english: Elements of Escape

verses.pali: “Pañcimā, bhikkhave, nissāraṇīyā dhātuyo.
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are these five elements of escape.

verses.pali: Katamā pañca?
verses.english: What five?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kāmaṁ manasikaroto kāmesu cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take a case where a mendicant focuses on sensual pleasures, but on that their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

verses.pali: Nekkhammaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto nekkhamme cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on renunciation, on that their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ kāmehi;
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from sensual pleasures.

verses.pali: ye ca kāmapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of sensual pleasures, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

verses.pali: Idamakkhātaṁ kāmānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: This is how the escape from sensual pleasures is explained.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno byāpādaṁ manasikaroto byāpāde cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on ill will, but their mind does not leap forth …

verses.pali: Abyāpādaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto abyāpāde cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on good will, their mind leaps forth …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ byāpādena;
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from ill will.

verses.pali: ye ca byāpādapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of ill will, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

verses.pali: Idamakkhātaṁ byāpādassa nissaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: This is how the escape from ill will is explained.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno vihesaṁ manasikaroto vihesāya cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on harming, but their mind does not leap forth …

verses.pali: Avihesaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto avihesāya cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on compassion, their mind leaps forth …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ vihesāya;
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from harming.

verses.pali: ye ca vihesāpaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of harming, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

verses.pali: Idamakkhātaṁ vihesāya nissaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: This is how the escape from harming is explained.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rūpaṁ manasikaroto rūpe cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take another case where a mendicant focuses on form, but their mind does not leap forth …

verses.pali: Arūpaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto arūpe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on the formless, their mind leaps forth …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ rūpehi;
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state … well detached from forms.

verses.pali: ye ca rūpapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of form, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

verses.pali: Idamakkhātaṁ rūpānaṁ nissaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: This is how the escape from forms is explained.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno sakkāyaṁ manasikaroto sakkāye cittaṁ na pakkhandati nappasīdati na santiṭṭhati na vimuccati.
verses.english: Take a case where a mendicant focuses on substantial reality, but their mind does not leap forth, gain confidence, settle down, and become decided.

verses.pali: Sakkāyanirodhaṁ kho panassa manasikaroto sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ pakkhandati pasīdati santiṭṭhati vimuccati.
verses.english: But when they focus on the cessation of substantial reality, their mind leaps forth, gains confidence, settles down, and becomes decided.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ cittaṁ sugataṁ subhāvitaṁ suvuṭṭhitaṁ suvimuttaṁ suvisaṁyuttaṁ sakkāyena;
verses.english: Their mind is in a good state, well developed, well risen, well freed, and well detached from substantial reality.

verses.pali: ye ca sakkāyapaccayā uppajjanti āsavā vighātapariḷāhā, mutto so tehi, na so taṁ vedanaṁ vediyati.
verses.english: They’re freed from the distressing and feverish defilements that arise because of substantial reality, so they don’t experience that kind of feeling.

verses.pali: Idamakkhātaṁ sakkāyassa nissaraṇaṁ.
verses.english: This is how the escape from substantial reality is explained.

verses.pali: Tassa kāmanandīpi nānuseti, byāpādanandīpi nānuseti, vihesānandīpi nānuseti, rūpanandīpi nānuseti, sakkāyanandīpi nānuseti so kāmanandiyāpi ananusayā, byāpādanandiyāpi ananusayā, vihesānandiyāpi ananusayā, rūpanandiyāpi ananusayā, sakkāyanandiyāpi ananusayā.
verses.english: Delight in sensual pleasures, ill will, harming, form, and substantial reality don’t linger within them.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhikkhu niranusayo, acchecchi taṇhaṁ, vivattayi saṁyojanaṁ, sammā mānābhisamayā antamakāsi dukkhassa.
verses.english: That’s why they’re called a mendicant who is without underlying tendencies, who has cut off craving, cast off the fetters, and by rightly comprehending conceit has made an end of suffering.

verses.pali: Imā kho, bhikkhave, pañca nissāraṇīyā dhātuyo”ti.
verses.english: These are the five elements of escape.”

verses.pali: Dasamaṁ.
Brāhmaṇavaggo pañcamo.
Tassuddānaṁ
Soṇo doṇo saṅgāravo,
Kāraṇapālī ca piṅgiyānī;
Supinā ca vassā vācā,
Kulaṁ nissāraṇīyena cāti.
Catuttho paṇṇāsako samatto.
